background_rationale: His career has been spent in foreign exchange payments and financial markets brokerage, from Global Currencies Ltd through leading StoneX's EMEA operations and its Commercial and Payments segments.

notable.summary: StoneX completed its acquisition of R.J. O'Brien, announced in 2025 at about $900 million in cash and stock, making it the largest non-bank futures commission merchant in the United States.
Reporting fiscal 2026 third-quarter results with net operating revenues up 47% year over year, Smith said the company was beginning to realize benefits from integrating R.J. O'Brien.
StoneX agreed to acquire Banco Travelex S.A., a Brazilian foreign exchange bank, subject to Central Bank of Brazil approval, excluding its retail FX operations.
StoneX announced the acquisition of Integra Trading S.A.S., establishing a Colombian coffee origination and processing platform.

personal_story.hook: He joined a British currency-payments firm in 1996; 28 years later he was running the global group that bought it.
personal_story.summary: Philip Smith earned a Bachelor of Science from Kent University, according to MarketsWiki. In 1996 he joined Global Currencies Ltd, a UK foreign-exchange payments company, and was elected to its board three years later. In 2004 the firm was acquired by the company now called StoneX, which, by former CEO Sean O'Connor's account, had begun his tenure with fewer than 10 people. Smith stayed on to run the acquired business, took charge of Europe, Middle East and Africa in 2008, and in December 2024, aged 52, succeeded O'Connor as Group CEO after more than 20 years working alongside him.
